content.thinking:
I'm planning the file structure using the builder API and prop conventions, designing a compact dungeon prop with a stone floor footprint.

Now I'm listing out the specific contents: barrels, crates, a chest, broken pillar, brazier with fire glow, skulls and bones, a candle, sacks, potions, shackles, a rusty sword, and a bucket, aiming to keep part count modest with reusable box-building helpers and consistent texture tiling.

Still writing palettes and texture generation logic...

Still writing hoop geometry... Then I move to the crate design: a main textured box with four darker corner posts and thin diagonal brace planks on the front and back faces.

For the chest, I'm deciding to make it open with a pile of gold inside rather than closed, so the body is a box and the lid tilts back on a rear hinge using a rotated box or arch-shaped extrusion, with the arch outline built from a half-circle polygon along the z-y plane.

Computing the lid's rotated position: pivoting -110° about the hinge axis, the center offsets to roughly (0, 0.94, -0.34) scaled by the half-length, giving a leaned-back open position. Part rotations use degrees on XYZ axes, so this should work directly.

Now for the brazier, I'm thinking of an iron bowl on tripod legs with pixel-style stepped flame shapes extruded in crossing directions (along x and z) to fake glowing fire, using varying column heights and glow colors to simulate flickering flame, centering the columns symmetrically around the bowl.

For the scene layout, I'm adding a ruined back wall with a stepped broken top, an iron-barred window made from rods, and a wall sconce holding a glowing torch flame to improve readability. I'm setting the floor at 2.8×2.4 centered at origin, with the wall placed along the back edge around z=-1.05 and given some thickness.

Now I'm breaking the wall into uneven brick sections of varying heights for a ruined look, adding a recessed dark panel with bars in front to suggest a barred window, and starting to place props like a chest and a cluster of barrels along the back-left area of the floor.

I'm simplifying the lying barrel idea since rotation handling is unclear, opting instead for three upright barrels of varying heights via scaled profiles. I'm also arranging stacked crates at the back-right with slight rotation offsets, and positioning a brazier toward the center-right of the scene.

Now I'm filling out the rest of the layout: a chest facing front, a second brazier, a skull pile with candle, a sack, potions resting on a crate top instead of a separate table, a sword stuck in the floor, a bucket, plus scattered bones and coins, a cobweb texture card in a corner, and hanging chains with shackles for detail. For the floor, I'm setting up a tiled stone texture using a repeating box tile scaled to match the room's proportions.

I'm building a flagstone floor from a grid of slightly offset stone boxes with small gaps between them sitting atop a dark base slab, then designing a matching flagstone texture tile with gray noise, cracks, and dithering to give the stones some visual variation.

Setting up a small helper utility to place textured boxes with randomized offsets and optional rotation, using a seeded RNG so the floor layout stays consistent, and reusing tile textures like IRON for metal variants instead of creating new dark-tinted tiles.

Planning out a plain-colored box helper too, while keeping a tight palette budget in mind, and sketching how the wood tile will vary plank-to-plank with grain intensity and dark seam rows using bayer dithering for texture.

For the gold pile, I'm combining small clustered gold spheres with coin-like cylinder discs, using a few gold tones for variety, sitting on a dithered gold base inside the chest interior.

Chest dimensions settle at 0.56 wide, 0.3 tall body, 0.34 deep, with a slightly raised gold interior box near the top rim and a squashed dome sphere (scaled flat and wide) placed above the body to suggest overflowing treasure, mostly embedded so only the top half shows.

Now I'm adding iron bands, corner brackets, a lock plate, and keyhole detail to the chest front, and working out a helper transform that rotates each part's local coordinates around the body's center so everything stays consistent with the chest's yaw rotation.

Still placing chest hardware...

Working through the rotation math confirms the lid's inner face tilts into view at -110 degrees, so I'll keep the same wood texture on all faces and thicken the bands to 0.07 so they're visible from both sides. Positioning the chest at yaw 0 near (0.6, ?, 0.4) for variety, then moving on to building a sword prop lying on the floor with a thin steel blade.

Defining the hilt, crossguard, and pommel dimensions...

Now I'm building the skull geometry with cranium spheres, jaw boxes, and dark eye sockets, plus a yaw-rotation helper for assembling a pile of four skulls, topped with a candle showing wax drips and a small glowing flame. Moving on to the brazier, I'm starting a lathe profile for the bowl shape.

Skipping the floor glow decal for now. I'm setting the brazier base to sit on the floor with the bowl positioned above it, then moving to the wall layout—dividing it into three sections (A, B, C) with different widths and heights to span the full 2.8 unit range, using stone tiles for the wall faces.

Now I'm adding detail elements: broken capstones on top of the middle section, scattered moss patches near the wall base, a recessed window with iron bars on section C, and a torch sconce bracket on section A.

I'm also hanging chain shackles from wall section B with alternating link orientations down to a cuff, and considering a textured cobweb plane in the corner between sections A and the floor.

For the web itself, I'm placing a small textured plane at the B/C wall junction and drawing a pixel-art cobweb radiating from the corner using manually computed ray angles per pixel.

Still defining the arcs and completing the ray pattern, then moving on to shape the sack as a lathed burlap profile with a tied knot, positioning it near the crates and brazier at the back left of the scene.

Now adding potions on top of a crate with lathed glass bottle profiles for red, green, and blue liquids with subtle glow, plus a corked top. I'm also considering scattering a few bones and coins near the chest for extra clutter detail.

Positioning three barrels around the scene with varying heights, giving one an open top with an inset lid ring to suggest dark liquid inside. Writing barrel profile function...

Still writing paint logic...

Now I'm defining a crate-building function with a wooden box body, corner posts, and diagonal corner braces positioned using the transform helper.

Still working out rotation math...

Now I'm figuring out the diagonal brace geometry so it spans the crate corners without overhanging—settling on a 38° angle and length of s*1.1 with 0.045 width, then placing the stacked crates with specific positions and rotations for the bottom and top boxes.

Adding crate C with potions on top, positioning a smaller crate D near the front, and nudging the sack and brazier placements to avoid overlapping—checking distances between the sack and brazier to confirm there's enough clearance. Then I'm laying out three potions on crate C's surface and starting to position the barrels.

Now I'm placing the chest, checking its width and depth against the barrel positions to avoid overlap, and figuring out the lid's extent toward the back. I'm also situating a torch above the barrels, plus a skull pile, a sword, and scattered skulls, while repositioning the brazier to keep everything clear of each other.

I'm adding a bucket near the floor, planning a wanted poster as a small pixel-art decal on the back wall with shackles nearby, and deciding where decals sit relative to the wall's front face. I'm weighing whether to skip extra details like a stone pillar or floor drain, but adding rubble stones and scattered bones near the wall base for texture, then setting up color constants for the iron materials.

Now I'm finishing out the color palette with brass, bone, wax, moss, rubble, potion, and steel tones, then laying out the floor flagstones as a grid of individual boxes with set dimensions sitting atop a dark base floor slab.

Writing flagstone texture logic...

Sketching out the poster's pixel grid...

Now I'm working out the torch flame shape, using stepped column profiles for an outer orange flame and smaller inner yellow flame, extruding them crosswise along two perpendicular directions with symmetric column widths centered around the torch axis.

For thickness, I'm making the inner yellow flame slightly thicker than the outer orange so it pokes through visibly on both faces, with directional thickness vectors computed via cross products for each extrusion axis. I'll wrap each extruded flame piece in a glow effect, and plan to add a small glowing box for the candle flame and tiny octahedron gems embedded in the gold chest piece.

Now I'm sketching helper functions like a `bone` function that draws a rod between two points with small sphere caps at each end, and reminding myself to keep imports clean to avoid unused-variable lint errors.

I'm finalizing the needed imports from the builder, math, and pixel/glow kits, skipping things like noise or mottle since I don't need them, and setting up constants for fillet size and texel scale before writing the quaternion helper function.

Adding box and tile-box helper functions...

Working out barrel wood paint logic...

Now I'm checking texel density to make sure the default paint size is sufficient for the total painted area, roughly estimating texels per meter rather than bumping up to a larger atlas unnecessarily.

Writing cell paint logic...

Defining color ramps for stone, wood, gold, sacking, and steel materials, then starting the wall tile texture generator...

Now building a wood plank texture, varying brightness by plank row and adding horizontal grain lines with occasional darker knots.

Now I'm placing nails at fixed positions on each plank row, then laying out the floor and tiling the flag crates across the grid so they cover the full scene bounds in both x and z.

I'm setting up the back wall using a sectioned helper function that places rectangular wall segments along z, with a wall texture stretched across tile steps. I'm realizing the wall face dimensions don't match the texture tile size cleanly, so I need to reconsider the texel scale to keep the texture looking consistent rather than oddly stretched.

Scaling up the wall tile to 64x96px with brick rows snapped to 16px and 8px steps so offsets align properly across rows, keeping the brick pattern from shifting out of alignment.

Now I'm sizing other tiles: flag texture to match floor face proportions, plank textures sized to fit crate and chest faces with lid and body dimensions proportioned correctly, then placing a strip of moss boxes along the wall base with randomized sizes, and adding broken stone caps along the top of the wall.

Now I'm adding smaller wall-cap boxes with varied heights, then building a window recess on the far wall with an iron frame made of top, bottom, and side boxes plus a few vertical bars.

Switching to the torch setup on wall A: I'm placing a small iron bracket, a holder cup, and a wooden torch shaft as separate boxes positioned against the wall.

Adding wrapped rags and a flame cell on top, plus an optional soot stain above it to mark where smoke would've scorched the wall. Now I'm setting up the shackle on wall B near x=-0.2, starting with the wall-mounted iron ring before working out the hanging chain links below it.

Continuing with the chain links alternating orientation down to a cuff at the bottom with a darker inner band, then duplicating the setup for a second chain and planning a poster placement nearby. Now I'm starting the brazier object, setting up its tripod legs around the base position.

Adding more geometry...

Adding floating ember particles above the coals, then sketching a skull-building function that places a scaled sphere for the cranium and small boxes for the eyes, oriented with a yaw-based transform.

Adjusting eye depth so they protrude slightly from the skull surface, then working out the skull pile arrangement with positions and yaw rotations for each skull, and placing a candle on top of the uppermost skull by calculating its cranium height and stacking the candle base accordingly.

Now I'm adding the flame glow, then scattering loose bones and a femur near the skull pile on the floor, and placing a sword with a thin steel blade propped nearby, checking that its bottom edge sits correctly relative to the floor height.

Continuing the sword, I'm building the guard, wooden hilt, and brass pommel, plus a thin dark fuller line down the blade for detail, and orienting the whole piece with a yaw rotation.

For the bucket, I'm now working out a lathe profile for a wooden vessel, defining the wall as a closed loop of points for the base, outer curve, and rim thickness.

Then I'm adding an iron hoop ring partway up the bucket using a flat rectangular loop, and sketching a handle as a thin bezier arc swept into a rod shape with the sweep function, though I'm skipping the water fill for now.

Adding water disc and sack geometry...

Adding coin color variation, then placing small red gem octahedrons scattered across the gold dome surface with a glow effect, sinking them slightly into the dome near center. I'm also considering adding a small chalice using a lathe geometry as an extra decorative piece.

Skipping scrolls and books on the crates for now, keeping the spider web but dropping rats. For rubble, I'm scattering small stone-pick shaped debris near the back wall base, randomizing size, rotation, and position while avoiding the bucket prop, using a palette of dark gray stone colors.

Now I'm double-checking the type signatures for the part-building helper functions — geometry, color/fill, scale, position, and quaternion options all line up correctly, and the rand function matches the expected signature. I'm verifying the lathe geometry options and confirming that the glow wrapper works properly whether given a lathe or a generic part, then double-checking that cell properties are read-only before moving into the cell paint logic.

Writing hash and flame functions...

Writing chest geometry code...

Adding the lid tilt with pitch rotation, placing the iron bands flush against the plank thickness, and checking the hinge geometry so the lid's rear edge doesn't clip through the rim wall when angled open.

I'm also scattering small brass rivets along the lid edges and adding corner plates and feet details, then moving on to defining the gem shapes starting with an octahedron.

I need to handle the step parameter carefully for TypeScript's optional property typing, building the options object conditionally so it only includes step when defined. Then I'll add the potion with a lathe-based glass shape and flat color glow, plus a cork, before writing out the full file.
